title: Free Transform Distort/Envelope warp not baked into published SWF (editor-only)
description:
Free Transform Distort and Envelope mesh warp (task 1219, commit ee7c148) is EDITOR-PREVIEW-ONLY and is silently DROPPED at SWF publish. The warp is correctly modeled and persisted (ShapeDisplayObject.warp / DrawingObject.warp in packages/core/src/engine/types.ts:398,595; whitelisted in updateDisplayObject packages/core/src/model/timeline.ts:8; written via Shell.tsx handleShapeWarp -> updateDisplayObject(... { warp })) and the editor canvas renders the warped geometry (packages/core/src/engine/renderer.ts:1574-1578,1601-1603 call warpShape(obj.shape, obj.warp, ...)). But the SWF compiler has ZERO knowledge of warp: grep -rniw "warp" packages/swf/src/ returns NOTHING (the only "envelope" hits are unrelated DefineSound sound-envelopes). The character pass encodes the ORIGINAL un-warped paths: packages/swf/src/compiler/characters.ts:260 calls encodeDefineShape4(charId, obj.shape, ...) -- obj.shape, never the warped geometry, and obj.warp is ignored. A PlaceObject2/3 matrix is affine and CANNOT represent a non-affine distort (perspective quad) or envelope (Coons/bezier mesh), so the published SWF shows the PRISTINE un-distorted shape.

FLASH PARITY: real Flash 8 BAKES distort/envelope into the actual DefineShape edge coordinates at publish (the warp becomes the shape geometry), since no matrix can carry it. We do not.

FIX DIRECTION: in the compiler character pass, when obj.warp is present, run warpShape(obj.shape, obj.warp, obj.x, obj.y) (engine/warp.ts) to produce warped stage-space paths and emit THOSE into DefineShape4 (subtracting the placement offset so the shape is origin-relative and the PlaceObject tx/ty stays the stage offset, per the CLAUDE.md shape-origin-normalization rule). Curves are already subdivided to chords by warpShape; the envelope Coons patch should likewise be sampled densely. Same handling needed for shape-tween (morph) start/end objs in characters.ts:210-211 if either carries a warp.

EVIDENCE: warp math itself is SOUND -- warp.test.ts (13 tests) passes; assertions are real geometric checks (perspective corner drag re-maps interior bilinearly; identity envelope reduces exactly to bilinear; bent-edge cubic midpoint rises 3/4*30=22.5; zero-area quad guarded, no NaN). The defect is purely the missing compile path, not the math.

VERDICT: real fidelity gap -- distort/envelope are invisible in the published movie.
